messages:
devin_runtime: Quick flag — seeing KV residency growth on gpu-pool-3 over the last ~2h. Longctx tenants' memory creeping, paging rate up, and tail latencies drifting. Suspect a noisy tenant spillover. Posting a tiny sample below.

kv_benchbot: perf-sample: 
```
kv-residency-sample {
  time: 2026-03-18T21:00:00Z
  tenant: acme-inc
  resident_pages: 18124
  reuse_rate: 0.12
  avg_kv_size_bytes: 3280
  pagewalks_5m: 4210
  paging_ops_5m: 920
}
```

sanjay: How correlated with sequence length distribution? Any sign of kernel selection fallback (like slower matmul path) causing CPU stalls that amplify residency churn?

devin_runtime: Good Q. From quick pprof: 99p seq >= 4096, bursts of short batches (<5) interleaved. Kernel selector fell back to generic_matmul on 2 nodes during those bursts — CPU stalls + more pagewalks. Hot loop is pagewalk + slab walking.

laura_ops: :thinking_face: Can we throttle that tenant or enforce soft quota? Current per-tenant soft quota is 6GB, but looks like fragmentation leaves holes so effective usable memory < quota.

kevin_sre: Pager spikes line up with autoscaler churn at ~21:02 UTC in logs. I think eviction thrash + fragmentation are amplifying each other — small free slabs lead to more pagewalks.

olivia_prodeng: Quick idea: try a rotational eviction policy (LRU + tenant round-robin age) to prevent one noisy tenant from hoarding fragmented slots. Any bench numbers on that pattern?

kv_benchbot: rotational-evict bench (micro): 
```
config: baseline (current LRU)
  tail_95_latency_ms: 87
  reuse_rate: 0.12
  pagewalks_5m: 4200

config: rotational-evict (LRU+round-robin tenant age)
  tail_95_latency_ms: 62  # -28%
  reuse_rate: 0.19        # +58% relative
  pagewalks_5m: 2900     # -31%
```

devin_runtime: Those numbers look promising. Caveat: rotational eviction can evict low-frequency but semantically important entries -> potential quality regressions (more recompute for some prompts).

sanjay: Proposal: combine per-tenant residency cap with adaptive rotational sampling. Add per-tenant `reuse_rate` metric; if reuse_rate < 0.2, shrink residency by a delta until reuse_rate stabilizes.

laura_ops: We can ship a soft throttle: bursty tenants get degraded to cheaper model variants (quantized or short-context variant) when they hit a longctx throttle. That reduces KV pressure while preserving availability.

kevin_sre: For immediate mitigation, I'll mark tenant `acme-inc` as `burst-limited` and patch eviction hook to aggressively evict pages older than 10m above the 90th percentile resident pages. Will monitor.

devin_runtime: Patch applied to staging. Observed ~30% drop in pagewalks within 15m and tail latencies improved by ~20%. Still need to validate under synthetic heavy-tail load.

olivia_prodeng: Can someone capture a 10-minute perf trace and also export the kernel-selector decisions for that window? I want to run the selector sim with the new distribution to ensure we don't regress kernel choices.

devin_runtime: On it — adding perf traces + pprof snapshot. I'll also dump per-tenant reuse_rate time series. Follow-up: let's put a short async doc with repro steps + config toggles to reproduce in local sim infra.

kevin_sre: FYI I'll add an alert for `pagewalk_rate > 2k/5m && reuse_rate < 0.15` so we get automatic paging mitigations next time. :white_check_mark:

laura_ops: Sounds good. After we validate, let's boil this down to a packaging change: (1) soft per-tenant residency knob, (2) adaptive rotational eviction, (3) optional auto-degrade to quantized variant. I'll draft runbook.

devin_runtime: Thanks all — tagging for follow-ups: @olivia_prodeng please open the eval, @sanjay please draft the adaptive sampling pseudocode, @kevin_sre monitor the alert. I'll upload traces in the thread.
